newsitem.title: UK: UK's Inntrepreneur says both shareholders committed.
newsitem.headline: UK's Inntrepreneur says both shareholders committed.

text.p: British pub chain the Inntrepreneur Pub Company, jointly owned by Grand Metropolitan Plc and Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd, said on Thursday shareholders were committed to the business.

"Neither shareholder is looking to exit from Inntrepreneur until they can realise the best value for their investment on behalf of their own shareholders," said Fiona Antcliff, a spokeswoman for Inntrepreneur company.
The proposed 24 billion pound merger between GrandMet and Guinness plc announced last month, to form GMG Brands, has led many analysts to think it will hasten GrandMet's eagerness to sell its stake.
Foster's chief executive Ted Kunkel told a news conference in Melbourne on Thursday that Foster's would continue to rebuild the value of the business until an acceptable offer came along.

"FBG did not state that its Inntrepreneur shareholding is currently on the market, rather FBG reitereated the public position, which both Inntrepreneur shareholders, that is FBG and GrandMNet, have taken for some time," said Antcliff.

"Both shareholders have stated publicly that Inntrepreneur is not a core business for either of them and both would seek appropriate exit routes once the new strategy which Inntrepreneur management has developed has been fully implemented and once all regulatory matters relating to Inntrepreneur have been resolved."

Foster's has first right of refusal on GMG's 50 percent stake in Inntrepreneur and vice versa. Inntrepreneur owns about 2,900 pubs and has property valued at 950 million pounds in Grandmet's 1996 accounts.
Inntrepreneur has been a challenge to both shareholders since its formation in 1991 and a range of uncertainties still remain.
The European Commission has yet to decide on whether the so-called tie can remain in place -- a system whereby pub companies compel their pub tenants to sell only beer supplied by them.
The tie is essential to Inntrepreneur's profits because if it remains the company can represent a sizeable estate, enabling it to negotiate big discounts from brewers of up to 90 pounds per barrel.
There is also a growing insurrection among pub tenants: 300 of them have began legal proceedings, who are witholding their rents and ignoring their beer supply tie.

In March, Britain's Department of Trade and Industry released Inntrepreneur from a 1991 undertaking to free all its pubs from the supply tie by March 1998. But many publicans claim they signed Inntrepreneur leases in the belief they will be free from the tie in March 1998.

In February, Inntrepreneur offered its tenants a base discount of 30 pounds a barrel on beer supplied by Scottish and Newcastle, which include Courage Best Bitter, Director's, John Smith's, Holsten, Budweiser and Foster's lager. Inntrepreneur said it would guarantee discounts until September 1998.
The company is tied into a supply agreement with S&N until March 1998, so it will have to fund the benefits until it can negotiate more favourable terms from other brewers.
